newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica sees higher exports from record sugar crop.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica sees higher exports from record sugar crop.

text.p: South Africa is on track to harvest a record 1997/98 cane crop yielding as much as 2.5 million tonnes of sugar, against 2.27 million in 1996/97, the South African Sugar Millers' Association said on Wednesday.
Chairman Don MacLeod told the organisation's annual meeting that exports were also expected to increase in the new season.
"The current season's initial production estimates are most encouraging and a record crop, which could be as high as 2.5 million tonnes, is anticipated," he said.

"Although the local market remains the bedrock of the industry, with the increase in production levels the quantity of sugar sold in the export market has become a high percentage of total sales. In the 1996/97 season 44 percent of all sugar produced was exported and early indications are that this will rise to 48 percent in the 1997/98 season."
Macleod said South Africa's political changes and the good quality of its sugar enabled the indsutry to widen its markets and export to more than 25 countries in 1996.
"The new premium destinations in Africa, the Middle East and Asia will continue to be supplied as the industry focuses on markets which offer better returns due to geographic and other advantages".
He said overall export earnings were expected to be 1.46 billion rand -- an increase of 271 million over the previous season.

But Macleod said the world sugar market remained a dump market and with higher crops predicted in major producers like Australia, Brazil and Thailand and world stocks at a high level, an increase in world prices in the near future was unlikely.
He said the local market price increased by five percent in April last year which was below inflation while local sales of 1.343 million tonnes were up 5.1 percent on the previous season.
"There was virtually no growth in the direct sales market but sales to the industrial market increased by 17 percent," Macleod said.
South Africa harvested its first good sugar cane after five years of drought last year.
